Let G be a prime graph. Every blowup of G is recolorable if and only if every induced subgraph of G is recolorable.

The paper labels this assertion Conjecture 1. Its results prove surrounding
modular-decomposition cases, not this equivalence for all prime graphs. The
target uses clique blowups; replacing vertices by independent sets would be a
different statement. Both directions of the equivalence and every induced
subgraph must be handled.
source_paper_text:
SOURCE: Manoj Belavadi, Kathie Cameron, and Ni Luh Dewi Sintiari,
"Recoloring modular graphs," Journal of Graph Theory 111(4) (2026), 113-123.
DOI: 10.1002/jgt.70005. First published 16 February 2026.
LICENSE: The version-of-record metadata gives CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. The full PDF is
not retained here; this file uses a bounded statement quotation and faithful
definition restatements.

DEFINITIONS (pages 2-3 of the version of record)

All graphs in the paper are finite and simple. A proper k-coloring of H maps
V(H) to {1,...,k} and gives adjacent vertices different colors. R_k(H) is the
graph whose vertices are the proper k-colorings of H, with two colorings
adjacent exactly when they differ on one vertex. H is recolorable when R_l(H)
is connected for every integer l>=chi(H)+1.

A nonempty set S of vertices is a module if every vertex outside S is adjacent
to either every vertex of S or no vertex of S. A nontrivial module has at least
two vertices and is a proper subset of V(H). A graph is prime if it has no
nontrivial module.

Substituting a graph J for a module S means deleting S, inserting J, and
joining every vertex of J to each outside vertex that had a neighbor in S.
A blowup is obtained by substituting a nonempty clique for each vertex; an
unchanged vertex corresponds to a one-vertex clique.

CANONICAL STATEMENT (Conjecture 1)

  Let G be a prime graph. Every blowup of G is recolorable if and only if every induced subgraph of G is recolorable.

STATUS AND TARGET BOUNDARY

The paper labels this assertion Conjecture 1. Its results prove surrounding
modular-decomposition cases, not this equivalence for all prime graphs. The
target uses clique blowups; replacing vertices by independent sets would be a
different statement. Both directions of the equivalence and every induced
subgraph must be handled.
target: Prove Conjecture 1 exactly: for every finite simple prime graph G, every blowup of G is recolorable if and only if every induced subgraph of G is recolorable; or give and rigorously verify an exact counterexample. Here R_k(H) has the proper k-colorings of H as vertices and joins colorings that differ on exactly one vertex; H is recolorable when R_l(H) is connected for every l >= chi(H)+1. A module is a nonempty vertex set whose outside vertices are each either complete or anticomplete to it, a prime graph has no nontrivial module, and a blowup substitutes a nonempty clique for each vertex.
title: Recolorability of blowups of prime graphs
